While some of it's individual parts and pieces aren't the best compared to the other Mother-likes of the past decade, the strength in this game lies in how well it ties everything together and manages to be significantly beefier than it's peer's content and length-wise. Even after 30+ hours, there's still more to discover with OMORI. And at the heart of it all is a surprisingly grounded emotional narrative that always felt honest with what it has to say. What else can I really ask for besides that?

This game changed my life. It's been over a year since I finished playing Omori and I still think about it every day. I had heard many good things about it and finally decided to play myself. Long enough to get you invested in the story and attached to the characters, the game makes some choices you have to make actually difficult for you. The characters are lovely and have gone/are going through things that many people have gone through, making them easy to relate to. Everything about this game is perfect in my opinion; the plot, the art, the characters and their backgrounds, the amazing soundtrack, and especially the message it conveys. It touches many sensitive subjects and depicts them in a beautiful way. I cried a lot while playing and afterwards as well. I highly recommend Omori as it is by far the best game I have ever played, though I do advise you to make sure you're in the right headspace since some choices and scenes are difficult to make and watch.

It's hard to say what makes this game special without giving too much away. So, I'll say this:

It's good. Real good. The game does a great job at subverting expectations and using symbolism. It's got an immediately recognizable art style along with a soundtrack that perfectly compliments exactly what is happening on screen. OMORI is certainly a one-of-a-kind experience, albeit not for everyone.

omori is very reminiscent of other story-centered rpg maker games but i think its long development time speaks for itself. aside from the routes and spaces, of which each takes a while to explore, there's a lot of extra content, optional quests, great attention to artistic and symbolic details, unique locations, and interesting story progression. plus very memorable soundtrack. the plot, art style, and characters are great. one of the games of all Time.

Best game I've ever played in my entire life. The connection you build with the characters is hard to put into words, the soundtrack is just perfect, the storytelling is out of this world, the art style is incredible. Dive in, and prepare to get emotional.

Many months after finishing OMORI, it has continued to live in my Headspace, rent free. I have yet to, and do not expect to, ever play a game that emotionally resonates with me like OMORI did. Regardless of where you are in life, OMORI team has a nuanced story to give to you that ranges everywhere on the emotional spectrum. These characters are some of my favorite I've ever met in a game and the visual presentation and incredible soundtrack perfectly matches the story of their friendship and how people can change, or not, all for better and for worse.
This game is beautiful, terrible and incredible.

Also gameplay wise it may not be THE BEST RPG battle system ever but it is very unique and super fun. I thoroughly enjoyed the Emotion and Follow Up mechanics and the latter especially brings the characters' personality into the battle system.

I recommend this game to everyone. 10/10.

At first i didn't really get this game and i found the huge map and lots of side quests and things to do a bit overwhelming. But holy hell does this game get fun and addictive later on. Also TW DON'T play this if you are sensitive to depression or selfdeleting content.

The art style is out of this world good, so much so that genuinely want to buy some of the official merch/prints.
The soundtrack is also amazing, all around this game really comes together with all of the small details that make it close to perfection.

One con that id like to point out is that the game renders in a smaller resolution box so if you're playing on a bigger monitor ( 31.5 inches ) with a higher resolution ( 1440p ) like me, it will be really shocking when you launch the game at first which is quite an immersion breaker for some. In that case i strongly suggest you upscale it trough the settings as much as you can and maybe check out a few mods like this one: .

All in all Great Game - 9/10 , it would be a 10 if they fix the screen issue, if that's even possible but id definitely recommend it if you like story rich games with a darker note.
